subproblems.title: Hilbert–Schmidt identity Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E² for an orthonormal basis f (reused accepted DAG theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form on ℝ^P = Euclid P) and let f = (f_0, …, f_{P−1}) be an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. Then Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(n−1)})² = n!·|α|_E². Here |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} and e is the standard basis of ℝ^P. (This is identity (★) of the parent proof. It is exactly the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis, reused with its identical frozen Lean type.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P)), ∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, (α (fun k => f (j k))) ^ 2 = (n.factorial : ℝ) * covectorEuclideanNorm α ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the identity (★) used in steps 4–5 of the parent proof (Fact (O) of the grandparent proof). It is exactly the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis (node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_sq_sum-a1, identical frozen type), and the proof below is the one accepted for that node (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3); coefficient norm of (6.1.5)/(6.1.15)). Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. For a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}). Let |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)²) and S_b(α) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(b∘j)². We must show S_f(α) = n!·|α|_E².
1. (Square of the norm.) The radicand Σ_I [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)² is a finite sum of nonnegative terms, so |α|_E² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² (Real.sq_sqrt).
2. (Basis independence by slotwise Parseval.) Let b, b' be orthonormal bases of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. For m = 0, 1, …, n put H_m := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(w_m(j))², where w_m(j)(k) := b_{j(k)} if k < m and w_m(j)(k) := b'_{j(k)} if k ≥ m. Then H_0 = S_{b'}(α) and H_n = S_b(α).
Fix m < n and split every j into its m-th value i := j(m) ∈ Fin P and its values j' on the other n − 1 slots. The map j ↦ (j(m), j') is a bijection (e.g. via Fin.insertNth / Fin.removeNth). For fixed j' let u_k := b_{j(k)} for k < m and u_k := b'_{j(k)} for k > m. Since α is multilinear, λ_{j'}(x) := α(u_0, …, u_{m−1}, x, u_{m+1}, …, u_{n−1}) is a linear functional of x ∈ ℝ^P. Write λ_{j'}(x) = ⟨r, x⟩ with r := Σ_a λ_{j'}(e_a) e_a. Parseval for orthonormal bases (OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_right) gives Σ_i λ_{j'}(b_i)² = ‖r‖² = Σ_i λ_{j'}(b'_i)².
The terms of H_{m+1} with fixed j' are exactly the λ_{j'}(b_i)² (i ∈ Fin P), and those of H_m are the λ_{j'}(b'_i)². Summing over j' gives H_{m+1} = H_m. By induction on m, S_b(α) = S_{b'}(α); in particular S_f(α) = S_e(α).
3. (Non-injective tuples.) If j is not injective, then e∘j is not injective (e is injective), so α(e∘j) = 0 because α is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective). Hence S_e(α) = Σ_{j injective} α(e∘j)².
4. (Injective tuples = increasing tuples × permutations.) Every injective j : Fin n → Fin P factors uniquely as j = I∘π with I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing and π ∈ Perm(Fin n).
Existence: with σ := Tuple.sort j, j∘σ is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing; take I := j∘σ and π := σ⁻¹.
Uniqueness: if I∘π = I'∘π' with I, I' strictly increasing, then I and I' have the same range. A strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is determined by its range, being the increasing enumeration of that n-element set (cf. StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT / Finset.orderEmbOfFin_unique), so I = I'. Then π = π' because I is injective.
Conversely, each such I∘π is injective. Thus (I, π) ↦ I∘π is a bijection from {I strictly increasing} × Perm(Fin n) onto {j injective}.
5. (Signs.) For I strictly increasing and π ∈ Perm(Fin n), α(e∘I∘π) = sign(π)·α(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap), so α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)².
6. (Counting.) By steps 3–5, S_e(α) = Σ_{I strictly increasing} Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} α(e∘I)² = |Perm(Fin n)|·Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² = n!·|α|_E² (Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin and step 1).
7. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 6, Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = S_f(α) = S_e(α) = n!·|α|_E². The same argument covers n = 0 (one empty tuple, which is strictly increasing; 0! = 1) and n > P (no injective and no strictly increasing tuples; both sides are 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: |α|_E² equals the sum of α(e∘I)² over strictly increasing I.
Slotwise Parseval (hybrid sums H_m) shows Σ_j α(b∘j)² is the same for every orthonormal basis b.
Non-injective tuples contribute 0; injective tuples are exactly I∘π (I increasing, π a permutation) and contribute α(e∘I)² each.
Counting the n! permutations gives Σ_j α(e∘j)² = n!·|α|_E², hence Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E².

subproblems.title: Evaluation on an orthonormal frame is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm (part (a); reused accepted DAG theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P = Euclid P. Then |α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1})| ≤ |α|_E, where |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α. (This is part (a) of the parent statement with β := α and v := τ. It is exactly the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le, reused with its identical frozen Lean type.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → |α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2 and 5 of the parent proof (its part (a)), written for α := β and τ := v. This is also the proof accepted for the DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_eval_le-a1 (declaration regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le, identical frozen type). Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P. For a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}), and let |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α. Uses the sibling sq_sum (regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis): for every orthonormal basis f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P), Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E² (★).
1. (n ≤ P.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so n = card(Fin n) ≤ finrank ℝ (Euclid P) = P (LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Let ι := Fin.castLE (n ≤ P) : Fin n → Fin P; ι is injective (Fin.castLE_injective) and (ι k : ℕ) = k.
2. (Orthonormal basis extending τ.) Define w : Fin P → ℝ^P by w(m) := τ(⟨m, h⟩) if h : (m : ℕ) < n, and w(m) := 0 otherwise. Let s := {m : Fin P | (m : ℕ) < n}. The restriction s.domRestrict w equals τ ∘ e, where e : s → Fin n, e(m) := ⟨m, m.2⟩, is injective; hence s.domRestrict w is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp). Since finrank ℝ (Euclid P) = P = card(Fin P), Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P) with f(m) = w(m) for all m ∈ s. In particular f(ι k) = τ_k for every k ∈ Fin n, because ι k ∈ s and w(ι k) = τ_k.
3. (Permuted frames.) For π ∈ Perm(Fin n), step 2 gives f∘(ι∘π) = τ∘π. Also α(τ∘π) = sign(π)·α(τ) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap). Since sign(π) = ±1, α(f∘(ι∘π))² = α(τ)².
4. (Comparison with the full sum.) The map Φ : Perm(Fin n) → (Fin n → Fin P), Φ(π) := ι∘π, is injective because ι is injective. Every term α(f∘j)² is ≥ 0. By step 3, n!·α(τ)² = Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} α(f∘Φ(π))² = Σ_{j ∈ image Φ} α(f∘j)² ≤ Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² (|Perm(Fin n)| = n! by Fintype.card_perm and Fintype.card_fin; Finset.sum_image; Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg).
5. (Apply (★).) By (★) for P, n, α and the basis f, the right-hand side equals n!·|α|_E². Since n! > 0, α(τ)² ≤ |α|_E².
6. (Conclusion.) Since |α|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), α(τ)² ≤ |α|_E² gives |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E (abs_le_of_sq_le_sq). ∎
proof_key_steps: Orthonormality gives n ≤ P; extend τ to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P with f∘castLE = τ.
Each of the n! permutation tuples castLE∘π contributes α(f∘castLE∘π)² = α(τ)², so n!·α(τ)² ≤ Σ_j α(f∘j)².
By (★) the full sum is n!·|α|_E²; cancel n! and take square roots: |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E.

subproblems.title: Pull-back by the coordinate map of an orthonormal frame preserves the Euclidean coefficient norm (part (b))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P = Euclid P, and let pL : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ be a continuous linear map with (pL x)_i = ⟨v_i, x⟩ for all x ∈ ℝ^P and i ∈ Fin n. Let l ∈ ℕ and let γ be an l-covector on ℝⁿ (Covector (Euclid n) l). Then the pulled-back covector γ∘pL = γ.compContinuousLinearMap pL, (γ∘pL)(u_1, …, u_l) = γ(pL u_1, …, pL u_l), satisfies |γ∘pL|_E = |γ|_E. Here |·|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm on Covector (Euclid P) l and on Covector (Euclid n) l respectively.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Euclid P) (pL : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid n), Orthonormal ℝ v → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (i : Fin n), pL x i = inner ℝ (v i) x) → ∀ (l : ℕ) (γ : Covector (Euclid n) l), covectorEuclideanNorm (γ.compContinuousLinearMap pL) = covectorEuclideanNorm γ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–4 of the parent proof (Fact (O), consequence (O3), of the grandparent proof). Step 4 of the parent proof concludes the equality |γ∘pL| = |γ| proved here.
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ, so (e_i)_k = 1 if k = i and 0 otherwise. For a family b : Fin m → E and j : Fin l → Fin m write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(l−1)}). Let |·|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm.
Uses the sibling sq_sum (regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis): for every m ∈ ℕ, every orthonormal basis b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin m) ℝ (Euclid m) and every l-covector α on ℝ^m, Σ_{j : Fin l → Fin m} α(b∘j)² = l!·|α|_E² (★).
Fix l and γ, and put α := γ∘pL ∈ Covector (Euclid P) l. Then α(u) = γ(pL∘u) for u : Fin l → ℝ^P (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply).
1. (n ≤ P.) v is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so n = card(Fin n) ≤ finrank ℝ (Euclid P) = P (LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Let ι := Fin.castLE (n ≤ P) : Fin n → Fin P; ι is injective (Fin.castLE_injective) and (ι k : ℕ) = k.
2. (Orthonormal basis extending v.) Define w : Fin P → ℝ^P by w(m) := v(⟨m, h⟩) if h : (m : ℕ) < n, and w(m) := 0 otherwise. Let s := {m : Fin P | (m : ℕ) < n}. The restriction s.domRestrict w equals v ∘ e, where e : s → Fin n, e(m) := ⟨m, m.2⟩, is injective; hence s.domRestrict w is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp). Since finrank ℝ (Euclid P) = P = card(Fin P), Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P) with f(m) = w(m) for all m ∈ s. In particular f(ι k) = v_k for every k ∈ Fin n.
3. (pL on the basis f.)
(i) Let i ∈ Fin n. For every k ∈ Fin n, (pL f(ι i))_k = ⟨v_k, f(ι i)⟩ = ⟨v_k, v_i⟩. By orthonormality of v (orthonormal_iff_ite) this is 1 if k = i and 0 otherwise, which is (e_i)_k (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply, single_apply). Hence pL(f(ι i)) = e_i by extensionality in Euclid n.
(ii) Let m ∈ Fin P with m ∉ range ι. For every k ∈ Fin n we have ι k ≠ m, so (pL f_m)_k = ⟨v_k, f_m⟩ = ⟨f(ι k), f_m⟩ = 0 because f is orthonormal (orthonormal_iff_ite applied to f.orthonormal). Hence pL(f_m) = 0.
4. (The two square sums agree.) Claim: Σ_{j : Fin l → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = Σ_{j' : Fin l → Fin n} γ(e∘j')². Let Φ : (Fin l → Fin n) → (Fin l → Fin P), Φ(j') := ι∘j'. Φ is injective because ι is: if ι∘a = ι∘b then a(k) = b(k) for every k.
(a) Let j ∉ range Φ. Then some k ∈ Fin l has j(k) ∉ range ι: otherwise, choosing for each k some j'(k) with ι(j'(k)) = j(k) gives j = Φ(j') ∈ range Φ. For this k, the k-th argument of γ in α(f∘j) = γ(pL f_{j(0)}, …, pL f_{j(l−1)}) is pL(f_{j(k)}) = 0 by step 3(ii). So α(f∘j) = 0 by multilinearity (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_coord_zero), and the term α(f∘j)² vanishes.
(b) For j' : Fin l → Fin n, step 3(i) gives α(f∘Φ(j')) = γ(pL f(ι j'(0)), …, pL f(ι j'(l−1))) = γ(e_{j'(0)}, …, e_{j'(l−1)}) = γ(e∘j').
Since Φ is injective and the terms off range Φ vanish by (a), the sum over all j equals Σ_{j'} α(f∘Φ(j'))², which is Σ_{j'} γ(e∘j')² by (b) (Fintype.sum_of_injective; equivalently Finset.sum_image together with Finset.sum_subset).
5. (Apply (★) twice.) (★) on ℝ^P with b := f and the l-covector α gives Σ_{j : Fin l → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = l!·|α|_E². (★) on ℝⁿ (m := n) with b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ and γ gives Σ_{j' : Fin l → Fin n} γ(e∘j')² = l!·|γ|_E². By step 4, l!·|α|_E² = l!·|γ|_E².
6. (Conclusion.) Since l! ≠ 0, |α|_E² = |γ|_E². Both norms are ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), so |γ∘pL|_E = |α|_E = |γ|_E (sq_eq_sq₀).
No case distinction is needed. For n = 0 < l both sums are 0: no tuple Fin l → Fin 0 exists, and every tuple Fin l → Fin P leaves the empty range of ι. For l = 0 both sums consist of the single empty tuple. ∎
proof_key_steps: Orthonormality gives n ≤ P; extend v to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P with f∘castLE = v.
pL maps f(castLE i) to e_i and every other basis vector f_m to 0.
Via the injection j' ↦ castLE∘j', Σ_j (γ∘pL)(f∘j)² = Σ_{j'} γ(e∘j')²; tuples leaving range castLE contribute 0.
Apply (★) on ℝ^P (basis f) and on ℝⁿ (standard basis): l!·|γ∘pL|² = l!·|γ|², hence |γ∘pL| = |γ|.
